5.text: From all this it may easily be concluded that it is no light matter to

6.text: collect the formulas of incantations from the Chukchee. I succeeded on

7.text: various occasions and in different localities in collecting about forty incantations,

8.text: which are given at the end of this chapter. Some of them are simply

9.text: formulas to be pronounced: others, evidently, are a kind of description as to

10.text: how the formula must be pronounced and acted upon.

11.text: The language of the incantations, on the whole, is the usual Chukchee:

12.text: but there are some obsolete words used in them, and there is even one the

13.text: meaning of which is already lost by the people. This proves that the words

14.text: of the formula have an equal importance with the action, and that, from

15.text: ancient times, there was a tendency toward consolidation and the exclusion

16.text: of any possible change. The general character, and even the details, of the

17.text: incantations, are the same throughout the whole Chukchee territory. Of the

18.text: reindeer-breeding incantations, those of the Kolyma country closely resemble

19.text: those of the Anadyr. The same may be said of the incantations relating to

20.text: the cure of diseases, to the protection against the coming-back of the dead, etc.

21.text: The supernatural powers mentioned in the incantations are the Upper

22.text: Being, the Sun, the Moon, various stars, among others the Pebbly River (the

23.text: Milky Way). The last was mentioned also in connection with shamanism,

24.text: though I could not collect any tales having a bearing on the personal character

26.text: Some of the short formulas are of a general character, and could have

27.text: been called simply prayers. For instance, a Chukchee, while sacrificing to

28.text: any of the spirits or “Beings,” will say, “Oh, let me look on (the world) for

29.text: a while!” or, “Let me walk around for a while!” or, “Receive my offering

30.text: and give me luck!” or “Let me take you for an assistant in my pursuits!”

33.text: The Chukchee, however, consider these formulas also as incantations,
